extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent owners, patent practitioners, and third-party reexamination requesters handling inter partes reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: MPEP guidance and procedural standards for conducting, merging, suspending, and appealing U.S. inter partes reexamination proceedings, including duties of disclosure, communications rules, handling of copending proceedings, and fee/petition treatments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to Federal Circuit — patent owner steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 CFR 1.983 and 37 CFR 41.81, a patent owner dissatisfied with the Board’s decision in a reexamination (commenced prior to Nov. 2, 2002) may appeal to the Federal Circuit after all parties’ rehearing rights are exhausted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The patent owner must (A) timely file a written notice of appeal in the Office addressed to the Director in accordance with 37 CFR 1.302 and 1.304 (preferably providing sufficient information for Director to determine whether to exercise the right), (B) in the Federal Circuit file a copy of the notice of appeal and pay the required fee under Federal Circuit rules, and (C) serve a copy of the notice of appeal on the third-party requester(s) in the manner provided in 37 CFR 1.248. A third-party requester is precluded from participating in any appeal taken by the patent owner to the Federal Circuit.

rubrics_metrics.name: No U.S. District Court action (35 U.S.C. 145) for inter partes reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The remedy by civil action under 35 U.S.C. 145 is not available to patent owners or third-party requesters in an inter partes reexamination proceeding; parties dissatisfied with Board decisions are limited to appeal to the Federal Circuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative history and MPEP note that 35 U.S.C. 145 (and limitations under MPEP §2279 for certain ex parte cases) were changed so that judicial review by civil action is not available for inter partes reexamination; district court proceedings are contrary to the goal of expeditious resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of disclosure in inter partes reexamination (37 CFR 1.933)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each individual associated with the patent owner in an inter partes reexamination has a duty of candor and good faith and must disclose to the Office all information known to be material to patentability as set forth in 37 CFR 1.555(a) and (b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The duty is satisfied by filing a paper complying with 1.555(a) and (b). Responsibility rests on the designated individuals; the Office will not evaluate compliance during the reexamination (questions will be noted as unresolved under 1.906(c)). Fraud, bad faith, or intentional noncompliance parallels the duty under 37 CFR 1.56 and may be noted if raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: No interviews on merits in inter partes reexamination (37 CFR 1.955)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews which discuss the merits of an inter partes reexamination proceeding are prohibited; there will be no inter partes or ex parte interviews discussing the substance of the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All communications regarding merits must be in writing and filed for entry into the record. Informal amendments by the patent owner that would be tantamount to ex parte interviews will not be accepted. Questions strictly about procedural matters (information obtainable by reading the file) may be discussed. Matters not available from the file are merits and may not be discussed. Examiners and merit-addressing staff must not make telephone calls for merits issues; paralegals or support staff may make limited calls for non-merits record-completion matters (these calls are not to be recorded on an interview summary and must be reflected in the next Office communication stating content was limited solely to the non-merits subject).

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone communications limited to non-merits and who may make them
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may, in its sole discretion, telephone a party only as to matters of completing or correcting the record where the subject does not go to the merits of the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such calls may be made by paralegals, Legal Instruments Examiners, or support staff, but not by the examiner or other Office employee who addresses the proceeding on its merits. If resolved by phone, the next Office communication should state the telephone content was limited to non-merits matters and 'nothing else was discussed.' Phone calls of this nature are not recorded on an interview summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of prior or concurrent proceedings (37 CFR 1.985) — patent owner duty
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner shall call the Office’s attention to any prior or concurrent proceedings involving the patent (e.g., interference, PTAB trial, reissue, reexamination, litigation) and the results of such proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes supplemental examination proceedings and PTAB reviews. The Office may accept copies of notices of suits and decisions for entry into the reexamination file to ensure updated status information. Non-merit court motions (venue, discovery dates, sanctions) will not be entered and will be expunged if entered inadvertently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party notification of concurrent proceedings limited to bare notice (37 CFR 1.985(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may file a paper notifying the Office of a prior or concurrent proceeding involving the same patent, but the paper must be limited to merely providing notice without discussion of issues in the current inter partes reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions that include arguments, discussions, or highlighting (underlining, fluorescent marks) go beyond bare notice and will be returned, expunged, or discarded at the Office’s discretion. Proper notice papers will be promptly entered into the reexamination record and considered when the proceeding next comes up for action on the merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office discretion to return/expunge voluminous or improper litigation submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may, in its sole discretion, return, expunge, or discard all or part of submissions from litigations or other proceedings if the volume is too extensive or the submission exceeds mere notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If returned, a party may limit the submission to what is deemed relevant and resubmit. Papers that provide party arguments (e.g., memoranda in support of summary judgment) will not be entered unless an entry right exists and must be submitted via the vehicle that provides that entry right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merger of concurrent reexamination proceedings (37 CFR 1.989)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reexamination is ordered while a prior inter partes reexamination is pending for the same patent and prosecution in the prior proceeding has not been terminated, the Office may merge the two proceedings or suspend one of them; merged proceedings normally result in issuance/publication of a single reexamination certificate under §1.997.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If merged with an ex parte reexamination, the merged proceeding is governed by §§1.902–1.997, except that rights of any third-party requester of the ex parte reexamination remain governed by §§1.510–1.560. Merger is discretionary and aimed at facilitating orderly handling and 'special dispatch.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of a second co-pending request and assignment guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The second request (Request 2) should be processed quickly and assigned to the same examiner as Request 1 when possible; if Request 2 is denied, Request 1 continues; if Request 2 is granted, the Office will not mail a first Office action with the order but will indicate that an Office action will follow in due course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When merger is ordered, prosecution will be conducted at the most advanced point possible for the first proceeding. If the first proceeding has a final rejection, prosecution will ordinarily be reopened to consider new patentability questions from Request 2, unless no new rejection or change of position is warranted. Patent owner will be given opportunity to respond prior to issuance of an Action Closing Prosecution (ACP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of identical claims in merged proceedings and remedy if not identical
rubrics_metrics.description: When proceedings are merged, the patent owner is required to maintain identical claims in both files while the proceedings remain merged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claims are not identical at the time the merger decision is drafted, an Office action will be issued concurrently with the merger decision containing a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) as indefinite, and will require a patent owner amendment to place claims in identical form. Patent owner must respond per 37 CFR 1.111 and include remarks setting forth the basis for any new or amended claims; third-party requester may comment on such amendments per 37 CFR 1.947.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing requirements in merged proceedings — single combined papers and signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: Responses/comments and other papers in a merged reexamination proceeding must consist of a single response/comment paper addressed to both files, filed in duplicate each bearing a signature, for entry in both files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All other papers filed in the merged proceeding are similarly required to be filed in duplicate for each file; the merger decision will point out these filing requirements and that both files are maintained as separate complete files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single examiner action and processing in merged proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: In merged prosecution, a single combined examiner’s action will be prepared and will include control numbers of both proceedings on every page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single action cover mailing sheet listing both control numbers will be used; technical support must ensure proper mailing to patent owner and each requester and scanning into the Image File Wrapper (IFW) database. When an NIRC is appropriate, notice will be printed for the merged proceeding and scanned into both merged files; CRU prepares the concurrent proceedings file per MPEP §2687 before release.

rubrics_metrics.name: When proceedings should not be merged — special dispatch requirement (35 U.S.C. 314(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings generally will not be merged if doing so would unduly delay the reexamination proceeding, because 35 U.S.C. 314(c) requires inter partes reexaminations to be conducted with 'special dispatch.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If merger would withdraw the first reexamination from its place in process and delay prosecution, non-merger is favored to allow first proceeding to conclude and second to be resolved separately. The Office retains authority to merge when merging would foster special dispatch; decisions are made case-by-case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees in merged proceedings — single fee suffices
rubrics_metrics.description: Where proceedings have been merged and a paper is filed that requires payment of a fee (excess claims, extension of time, petition, appeal, brief, oral hearing, etc.), only a single fee need be paid for the merged proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, one fee suffices for the patent owner’s appellant brief in merged multiple proceedings even though copies must be filed for each file in the merged proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions to merge multiple copending reexamination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: No petition to merge is necessary because the Office will generally sua sponte decide whether to merge; premature petitions filed before order to reexamine the second request will be returned and noted in both files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner may file a petition to merge at any time after the order to reexamine the second request. Acceptance of such a petition after the order but prior to issuance of first Office action requires a waiver of 37 CFR 1.939 and is used to assure early merger. A third-party requester of reexamination #1 does not have standing to file a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 to merge with reexamination #2 if it lacks standing with respect to #2; the requester may instead file a notification under 37 CFR 1.985(b) and may petition to stay the proceeding it requested under 37 CFR 1.182.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision authority for petitions to merge
rubrics_metrics.description: All decisions on the merits of petitions to merge multiple reexamination proceedings where at least one is an inter partes reexamination will be made by OPLA; decisions where none is inter partes will be made by the CRU Director or delegated CRU SPRS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This assigns internal Office responsibility for merger decisions based on the type of reexamination involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of concurrent interference and inter partes reexamination (37 CFR 1.993)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent undergoing inter partes reexamination is or becomes involved in an interference or PTAB trial, the Director may suspend the inter partes reexamination, the interference, or the trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director will not consider a request to suspend an interference or trial unless a motion under 37 CFR 41.121(a)(3) to suspend has been presented to and denied by an administrative patent judge and the request is filed within ten days of the APJ’s denial (or other APJ-set time). Suspension is generally disfavored because reexaminations must proceed with special dispatch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory notices for appeals/contested cases (37 CFR 41.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: In an appeal brief or at initiation of a contested case and within 20 days of any change, a party must identify (1) its real party-in-interest and (2) each judicial or administrative proceeding that could affect or be affected by the Board proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For contested cases, a party seeking judicial review must file a notice with the Board of the judicial review within 20 days of filing the complaint or notice of appeal and include a copy of that complaint or notice of appeal. See also 37 CFR §§1.301–1.304.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of examination before initiation of contested case (37 CFR 41.102)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before a contested case is initiated (unless the Board otherwise authorizes), for each involved application and patent examination or reexamination must be completed and there must be at least one claim that (1) is patentable but for a judgment in the contested case and (2) would be involved in the contested case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures there is a live patentability issue and at least one claim that would be implicated by the contested case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board jurisdiction over involved files (37 CFR 41.103)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board acquires jurisdiction over any involved file when the Board initiates a contested case and other proceedings for the involved file within the Office are suspended except as the Board may order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives the Board flexibility to tailor solutions when reexamination and interference/trial proceedings are copending; reexamination proceedings themselves cannot be involved in an interference (reexamination is neither an application nor a patent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to suspend interference pending reexamination (37 CFR 41.121(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A miscellaneous motion under 37 CFR 41.121(a)(3) to suspend an interference pending the outcome of a reexamination may be made at any time during the interference by any party, presented to the APJ who will decide based on facts, but suspension is not favored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normally the motion will not be considered until a reexamination order is issued, and suspension usually will not be permitted until motions in the interference are disposed of. If APJ denies the motion, a request to stay the interference may be made to the Director under 37 CFR 1.993; the Director’s decision will be made by the Chief APJ of the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination requests filed during an interference — patent owner notice and processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.913 and 41.8(a), if a request for inter partes reexamination is filed during the enforceability period of a patent, the patent owner must notify the Board within twenty days of receiving notice of the request; such requests will be processed normally and generally will not delay the reexamination when the third-party requester is not a party to the interference or fails to timely petition for a stay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner, in reexamination, rejects a patent claim corresponding to a count in the interference, the attention of the Board shall be called to that rejection. The Office will generally proceed with required decisions in reexamination and, as appropriate, forward status to the interference.
